theme: Reviewing what matters with too few reviewers
title: Reviewing What Matters With Too Few Reviewers
strategies: do nothing: send everything to the fixed auto-moderation rule (reproduces the evaluator's own do-nothing anchor)

score-ranked routing: review the model's most-confident predicted violations first, filling one reviewer to capacity before the next -- ignores severity, appeal cost, and ambiguity, and burns fresh reviewer capacity on cases the auto-rule was already likely to get right

expected-harm x uncertainty routing with reviewer rotation: estimate each item's expected cost reduction from review (using model_score as a violation-probability estimate, weighted by category severity/appeal cost and item ambiguity), skip items where review is expected to hurt, and round-robin the chosen items across reviewers sorted by accuracy so no reviewer absorbs a long fatiguing run
local refinement: start from a value-ranked assignment and swap/reorder within and across reviewer queues (seeded, deterministic) to further reduce realized expected cost
